claim: Dynamically dispatching annotation tasks by synthesizing performance history, cost analysis, and quality feedback to assign each sample to the most suitable annotator achieves an optimal trade-off between label quality and annotation cost.
falsifier: Implement a scheduling agent that uses performance history, cost analysis, and quality feedback to assign tasks to annotators, and measure the resulting label quality and annotation cost compared to fixed assignment or other baselines.

conditions: multi-source annotators including LLMs, SLMs, and human experts
scheduling agent synthesizes performance history, cost analysis, and quality feedback

title: Dynamic task dispatch based for optimal trade-off between label

claim: A single search chain-of-thought stage is insufficient for precise localization in aerial vision-and-dialog navigation; additional fine-grained verification is required.
falsifier: One could evaluate a system with only a search CoT stage on aerial navigation benchmarks and measure localization accuracy, then compare with a system that adds a confirmation stage.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Single search chain-of-thought stage–precise localization boundary
